tactic.explain.counter_532: Five at the back and a low, very compact block (pressing low, line low). When the ball is won, it goes quickly and deep (tempo high) to the two strikers, and the wing-backs join late. In the simulation: strong when you are the weaker side; the risk is that the opponent gets a lot of the ball and the strikers are on their own. Use it away or against a team that attacks a lot.
tactic.explain.flankdruk_352: Three centre-backs, with wing-backs who press hard on the flanks (high block, pressing high). Two strikers close off the middle. In the simulation: strong against teams that build up wide; the risk is the space behind the wing-backs. After minute 75 with a lead it drops to a low block. Use it when you want to take the ball high up the pitch.
tactic.explain.hoge_druk_433: The highest block and the most pressing of the starters: the team wins the ball back right after losing it, and presses when the ball goes back to the keeper. In the simulation: strong against teams that build up slowly; the risk is a lot of space behind the defence and tired legs. After minute 70 with a lead it drops to a mid block. Use it when you have the stronger team.
tactic.explain.laag_blok_442: Two compact lines of four deep in your own half (low block, very compact, little pressing). The two strikers keep the space in front of the ball closed, and the wingers counter wide. In the simulation: strong because the opponent finds little room; the risk is that you rarely have the ball. Use it as the weaker side, or to defend a lead.
tactic.explain.lange_bal_442: A compact mid block with two lines of four. Out of the back the ball goes long and directly to the target man, and the others run for the second ball. In the simulation: strong against teams that press high; the risk is giving the ball away often and not keeping it. Use it when building up short is not working.
tactic.explain.man_om_man_433: Experimental: often gives lopsided matches (very high scores and shot counts). Every defender marks one opponent over the whole pitch (man marking, pressing very high). In the simulation: strong when your players are fitter than theirs; the risk is that one lost duel opens a gap, and that it costs a lot of energy. From minute 60 with a lead, or when tired, it drops to a low block. Use it for a short, intense game.
tactic.explain.positiespel_4231: Slow, patient play (tempo low) to keep the ball: the full-backs stay wide, the holding midfielders drop into the build-up, and the wingers cut inside. Without the ball it defends in a mid block. In the simulation: strong because you control the match; the risk is losing the ball in your own half and slow play when you are behind. Use it when your team is better on the ball.
tactic.explain.vleugelspel_433: Wide play: the wingers stay on the touchline, the full-backs overlap, and the striker and a midfielder run into the box. Without the ball it defends in a mid block. In the simulation: strong against a narrow defence; the risk is that the middle is thin and crosses can be easy to defend. Use it when you have fast wingers.
tactic.explain.testcase_a_433: A fictional test tactic with a high block and a lot of pressing (pressing high, tempo high, mixed pressing). It presses when the ball goes to the flank and when the opponent receives badly. With a lead from the second half, or when tired, it drops to a low block. In the simulation: strong at winning the ball high; the risk is space behind. Use it to compare against your own tactic.

help.title: About this screen
welcome.title: Welcome to Gaffer's Notebook
welcome.game: You are the coach in the dugout. Design tactics, watch your team play, take on challenges and play a league season. Your decisions shape the match.
welcome.keys:
Space - pause · B - substitutions and tactics · Esc - settings and home
F11 - fullscreen · F1 - help · F9 - feedback
welcome.early: Open beta. Matches usually take 4–5 minutes, plus pauses. AI and balance are still being tested. Report problems through Feedback (F9).
onboarding.title: Your first steps
onboarding.step.substitution: 2. Make a substitution in a match (B)
onboarding.step.tactic: 3. Create and save your own tactic
onboarding.step.meter: 4. Compare two tactics in the meter
help.menu.1: You are the coach: your tactics guide the players.
help.menu.2: Kick off plays a full match in about 4–5 real minutes. Challenges offer specific goals; Play live lets you coach each match.
help.menu.3: The checklist records five things to try. Go there opens the relevant screen.
help.menu.4: Esc opens all settings, including language, match length, display and feedback. Tactic library lists all tactics with favourites, rename, delete, import and export.
help.challenges.1: Challenges give your tactic a concrete goal over several matches.
help.challenges.2: Try Break down the block with Positional play 4-2-3-1. Read the goals first.
help.challenges.3: Choose your tactic and team level, then Play live. B opens substitutions during the match.
help.challenges.4: Finish a match and continue to see your progress. Simulate all runs the whole challenge for you. Cancel stops a simulation or opponent preparation without saving a result.
help.editor.1: The Tactic maker lets you design how your team plays.
help.editor.2: Open a tactic or choose New and a formation. Select a phase above the pitch.
help.editor.3:
Drag a player, or select one, to change a role or instruction (hover for an explanation). Drag a rectangle on an empty spot, or Shift+click, to select several players and move them together.
Arrow keys move the selection 1 m (Shift: 5 m). G snaps to a 2.5 m grid. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes.
L shows the runs of the selected players, P (▶ Show movement) plays them. The TEST tab plays a quick test.
help.editor.4: Enter a new filename and Save. Compare it with the original in the meter. Open → Export file shares a JSON file with friends; Open → Import file opens theirs. Save after importing to keep your own copy.
help.meter.1: The Tactic meter compares two tactics over repeated matches, swapping home and away.
help.meter.2: Choose your saved tactic as A and the original as B, then Compare. Wait for the report.
help.meter.3: Read wins, draws and losses, then the differences and heatmaps to see what changed.
help.meter.4: The meter starts a comparison when opened. Cancel stops it; then choose tactics and Compare to restart. Results describe these matches; they are not a guarantee.
help.season.1: League is a season with a table, fixtures and promotion or relegation.
help.season.2: Choose a tactic for the next match, then play live or simulate a round.
help.season.3: In a live match, B opens substitutions and Space pauses. Finish the match and return here.
help.season.4: Read the table and schedule after the round. Your career is saved automatically.
help.squad.1: Squad shows your players and how well they understand the chosen tactic.
help.squad.2: Choose a team level and tactic to inspect the players and reserves.
help.squad.3: Look at the demands and familiarity before training a concept.
help.squad.4: Learning is limited per period. Try a simpler tactic if the demands are too high.
season.familiarity_warning: Your tactic is too demanding for your squad. Choose a simpler tactic or train.
feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.intro: Tell the maker what happened or what you think. A zip file is saved on your desktop; nothing is sent. You can open the zip and check it before you send it yourself.
feedback.contents: It contains a screenshot of this window, the game log, version and system type (Windows, processor, memory), your progress files and your note.
feedback.note_placeholder: What happened, or what did you expect?
feedback.saved_hint: Nothing has been sent. Send this file to the maker yourself.
feedback.failed: The feedback file could not be saved: {0}
feedback.error_body: The game ran into an unexpected problem. You can usually keep playing. A feedback file helps the maker to fix it; nothing is sent automatically.
match.speed.title: MATCH LENGTH
match.speed.help: About 4–5 minutes at the standard pace; pauses add time. B pauses at the next break for coaching. The full 90 minutes are simulated.
settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Game, display and navigation in one place. The match pauses while this page is open.
settings.pace_hint: All 90 football minutes are simulated. Pauses add time; the chosen pace also applies to your current match.
settings.language_hint: Language changes take effect when you return to the home screen. On the home screen, close Settings to apply them.
settings.display_hint: You can resize the game window by dragging its edge. The game starts in fullscreen; F11 switches between fullscreen and windowed, and your choice is remembered.
settings.controls: Esc: settings / back. Space: pause match. B: coaching at the next break. End: calculate the remaining match. F1: screen help. F9: feedback.
settings.feedback_hint: Feedback creates a local package with your note, screenshot, logs and progress. Nothing is sent automatically.
settings.save_failed: Active for this session, but saving failed. Check write access to your progress folder.
settings.leave_warning: Return home? The current match or challenge will stop. Results that have not been saved will be lost.
settings.quit_warning: Quit the game? The current match or calculation will stop. Saved progress will remain.
help.match.1: Your tactics guide the players. Standard matches take about 4–5 real minutes; pauses add time.
help.match.2: Space pauses immediately. B opens coaching and substitutions at the next break in play.
help.match.3: Esc opens Settings without leaving your match. Change match length, display or popup preferences there.
help.match.4: End calculates the remaining match. The end card shows the result, statistics and pitch coverage.
settings.adaptive_hint: In the competition, prof and (some) semi-pro opponents change their tactic after you played the same style three times. The reason is shown before the match.
opponent.adapt.high_press: Opponent expects high pressing: plays long balls behind your line.
opponent.adapt.possession: Opponent expects you to keep the ball: defends in a compact low block.
opponent.adapt.low_block: Opponent expects a deep block from you: presses high to win the ball early.
settings.audio_hint: Sound effects are generated for this game; music credits are in About. Changes apply at once.
tour.skip_hint: Esc also skips. Restart it any time from Settings > Help and feedback.
tour.restart_later: The tour starts again on the home screen and in your next match.
tour.menu.intro.title: Welcome, coach
tour.menu.intro.text: You draw up the plan, watch your team play and steer at breaks in play. This short tour shows the way round.
tour.menu.tactics.title: Choose your tactics
tour.menu.tactics.text: Pick a tactic and level for both sides here. The bars show the style of each plan.
tour.menu.editor.title: Make your own plan
tour.menu.editor.text: The Tactic maker lets you change formations, roles and team settings. Save it and it appears in the list.
tour.menu.start.title: Your first match
tour.menu.start.text: Kick off here or press Enter. A match takes about 4 to 5 minutes.
tour.menu.meter.title: The meter
tour.menu.meter.text: The meter plays two tactics against each other many times. It shows how they compare.
tour.menu.steps.title: Your first steps
tour.menu.steps.text: This list tracks what you have tried, in any order. Esc opens Settings, where you can restart this tour.
tour.match.coach.title: Coach with B
tour.match.coach.text: Press B to make substitutions and tactic changes at the next break in play. Space pauses, Esc opens Settings.
tour.match.endcard.title: Read the end card
tour.match.endcard.text: The score, the statistics per team and the heatmaps show how your plan worked out. Play again or try another tactic.

about.disclaimer: Not endorsed by any data provider. All clubs, players and seasons are fictional.
about.provisional.head: Provisional parts (v0)
about.provisional: League: clubs, levels and the promotion and relegation rules may still change; all clubs are fictional. Squad: player levels, training and tactical understanding are a working hypothesis and not calibrated against real data yet.
about.privacy.head: Privacy
about.privacy: The game does not use the internet and sends nothing automatically. Your progress and settings stay on this computer.
about.community.head: Community
about.community: Questions, feedback, tactics and bug reports are welcome on the Discord server. The button opens your browser; the game itself sends nothing.
about.licenses.head: Licence files
about.licenses: The full licence texts are in the files next to the game: GODOT_LICENSES.txt, DOTNET_LICENSE.txt, DOTNET_THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt, FONT_OFL.txt, WYSCOuT_NOTICE.txt, BRONNEN_NOTICE.txt (DFL and SkillCorner) and MUSIC_CREDITS.txt.

editor.setpieces_help: Choose what your team does at corners and free kicks. 'As in open play' leaves a situation alone.
editor.sp_explain.current: Nothing special: the players keep their normal positions.
editor.sp_explain.korte_paal: Your best headers wait at the near post; the corner is lofted into that zone.
editor.sp_explain.verre_paal: Your best headers wait at the far post; the corner is lofted over to them.
editor.sp_explain.kort: The corner is played short to a team-mate who drops next to the taker.
editor.sp_explain.penaltystip: Your best headers gather around the penalty spot; the corner is lofted there.
editor.sp_explain.voorzet: The free kick is lofted into the box where your best headers wait.
editor.sp_explain.schot: Shoot straight at goal from within 25 metres; further out it becomes a cross.
editor.sp_explain.zone: Defenders guard areas: four on the six-yard line and two around the penalty spot.
editor.sp_explain.man: Every attacker in the penalty area gets a defender, one metre goal-side of him.
editor.sp_explain.palen: How many defenders stand on the goalposts (0, 1 or 2).
